finding: The prior control-plane candidate added durable activation consumption, replay protection, supervisor STATE, and health-witness LOGIC, and the prior checker + advisor accepted 'detached continuation'. But mechanically: supervisor.mjs spawns NO OS process; executeSupervisedRun does `await executeSignedRun(...)` synchronously in the LAUNCHER process (run-five-hour.mjs:274); there is NO dedicated supervisor process entry point and NO independent witness process entry point. The prior acceptance-matrix row CP-25 honestly labeled OS detachment 'production-only behavior ... modeled via durable receipt' — i.e., MODELED_ONLY, not proven.
remediation: Implement a REAL dedicated supervisor OS process (supervisor-main.mjs) spawned detached by the launcher, and a separate read-only witness process (witness-main.mjs). The launcher validates + atomically consumes + spawns ONE detached supervisor + waits bounded for RUN_ACTIVE + returns a receipt + EXITS (never awaits the job run). Prove with REAL-process deterministic stub tests (different PIDs, launcher exits, supervisor survives + heartbeat advances, separate witness attaches, provider-stub descends from supervisor, process-group teardown). No real Claude, no real activation, no real run.
